instruction: Correct the orientation of the inverted video and save it as 'Macintosh_Ad_1984.mp4' on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Variation 2: Check if the saved video file exists and has a reasonable file size (2-4 MB range, similar to the source video which is ~3MB). This verifies the agent successfully processed and saved the video.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical verification gap: Evaluator only checks file size, not whether orientation was actually corrected
Incomplete coverage: Instruction requires verifying orientation correction, but evaluator only verifies file existence and approximate size
High false positive risk: Would pass if agent simply renamed the file, copied any ~3MB video, or created corrupted file in size range
Semantic mismatch: File size cannot semantically verify that video orientation was corrected - requires video metadata analysis or frame inspection
Does not verify core requirement: The main task is orientation correction, not just saving a file of a certain size
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use video metadata analysis to check rotation/orientation tags (e.g., ffprobe to check video rotation metadata)
Compare video rotation metadata between source and output files to verify orientation was changed
Use video frame analysis to detect if frames are properly oriented (e.g., extract first frame and check orientation)
Add checksum or content verification to ensure output is derived from source video, not a random file
Consider using ffmpeg/ffprobe to verify: (1) file is valid video, (2) has correct rotation metadata, (3) dimensions match expected orientation
